newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn confident EMU stability pact to be agreed.
newsitem.headline: Bonn confident EMU stability pact to be agreed.

text.p: The German finance ministry said on Wednesday that the Bonn government remains confident European Union members will agree to create a "stability pact" to enforce adherence to monetary union criteria.
Commenting on press reports that Germany might be ready to accept a delay in introducing a single European currency, slated for 1999, the ministry said the question had not been posed.

It added work was continuing on the details of a stability pact which, in part, would set up a framework for sanctions against EMU members that allow budget deficits and public debt to exceed the strict criteria set out in the Maastricht Treaty.
Germany has been in dispute with other EU members over the nature of the sanctions and whether they would be virtually automatic, which some EU members oppose.
Juergen Stark, state secretary in the finance ministry, has said Germany would not agree to a watered-down stability pact.
